title: cli: a flag value that begins with '-' plus a declared short char (e.g. an id '-yQ9…') is refused as 'Flag --id expects a value', so such rows can never be bound
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cw787kMeaX7oyz7DDC

Found while fixing #32976 (PR #33426, which only makes the test seed fixed ids and does not touch this). Measured at `01321f651` against `packages/cli/bin/run-dev.js`.

## Line

`os migrate stored-references bind` (and any CLI command with a short-char flag) · a string flag whose value is a driver-minted id · 1 in 4096 rows for `bind` · measured.

```
os migrate stored-references bind --table sys_sharing_rule --id -yQ9zzAbCdEfGhIj --package com.example.crm --yes --json
→ objectstack: INVOCATION ERROR — Flag --id expects a value   (exit 2, 0 bytes on stdout under --json)
```

The `--id=-yQ9zzAbCdEfGhIj` spelling fails the same way. The SQL driver mints row ids as `nanoid(16)`, and that alphabet contains `-`. oclif 5.1.2 `parseFlag` refuses a value that `findFlag` resolves to a declared flag, and `findShortFlag` reads only the second character. `bind` declares `--yes` as `-y`, so any stored row whose id begins `-y` can never be bound, in any spelling. A sweep of all 4096 two-character prefixes after `-` through the bind's real flag set refused exactly 64, all of them `-y`.

## Family

Any CLI string flag that can carry a minted id or other user value, on a command that declares a short char. By grep over `packages/cli/src/commands`: 27 commands declare `-y`, 26 `-t`, 23 `-u`, 16 `-f`.

## Do

- Decide the fix at the family level (for example, a shared value-flag helper or a parse hook that accepts a dash-leading value for flags typed as an id, or upstream oclif behaviour), not per command.
- Pin by enumeration: walk every command's declared string flags and assert that a value beginning `-<declared char>` parses as a value. Ablate.

Reader who acts: `packages/cli/src/commands/**`, oclif flag parsing in `packages/cli`.
Suggested grade: p3. Lane: `domain:server`.
